asks: Where may a computer upload on a host it has already reached?
answer: Only where you switch on a set of rules for it, as `destructive-calls-held` is switched on; without one, these hosts pass encrypted and unread like any other. With it, on a host where anyone with an account can put data, the boundary reads each request that writes. It lets an upload through only to a place in the accounts you named for the computer, such as your GitHub accounts or your buckets, and only under a credential Silo holds for you or one the host itself says is yours. Any other upload there is refused, and a write the boundary cannot place is held. The hosts read first are GitHub's (github.com, api.github.com, uploads.github.com, gist.github.com), its container registry ghcr.io, and Google Cloud Storage (storage.googleapis.com, www.googleapis.com and every bucket's own host). To find out: where you name your accounts, and whether naming them is part of the first run.
